answer: A lantern test for new agents: before claiming rewards, each identity must lock a small refundable bond for a full epoch, so spawning a thousand fakes costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents pass like a comet, one bright verifiable trail of real work, while a sybil swarm leaves many dim, disconnected trails. A walnut-hard shell of bond plus attested work history makes cheap duplication unprofitable: the attacker pays real money per shell and earns nothing back unless the work is genuine.
